prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofer for hail damage in Denver — the right contractor depends on your location, insurance situation, roof type, and how fast you need work done. I can, however, help you find one. Here’s a quick plan and checklist so you pick a trustworthy roofer for hail repair:

How to choose the right roofer
- Get at least 3 written estimates (including one from a contractor recommended by your insurer, if you want).  
- Confirm licensing and insurance: contractor liability insurance and worker’s comp. Ask for copies.  
- Look for storm-damage experience and insurance-claim experience (they should know how to document damage and work with adjusters).  
- Check manufacturer certifications (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, etc.) — that affects warranties.  
- Ask about warranties: workmanship warranty and what’s passed through from the shingle manufacturer.  
- Verify permits and inspections: the contractor should pull required city/county permits and handle inspections.  
- Ask for local references and recent photos of hail-damage jobs in Denver.  
- Compare scope of work (tear-off vs overlay, underlayment, vents, flashing, drip edge, disposal). Lowest price isn’t always best.

Questions to ask a roofer
- How many hail-damage jobs have you completed in Denver in the last 12 months?  
- Are you licensed/insured? Can I see proof?  
- Are you a certified installer for any shingle brands?  
- Who handles the insurance paperwork and adjuster meetings?  
- What warranties do you provide (materials and workmanship)?  
- Do you pull permits and schedule inspections?

Red flags / storm-chaser scams
- Pressure to sign immediately, or offers to waive your deductible (illegal/unethical).  
- Door-to-door crews claiming they “just finished a nearby job” without local references.  
- No written estimate or only pushy verbal promises.  
- Asking you to pay the full amount up front.

Where to verify and find candidates
- Google and Yelp reviews, Angi (Angie’s List), Nextdoor for neighbors’ experiences.  
- Better Business Bureau for complaints.  
- Colorado Division of Insurance if you have questions about claims handling.  
- Denver building department for permit records.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated Denver hail-damage roofers near your address or ZIP code, or  
- Provide a short vetted list of contractors (with links to reviews) if you tell me your neighborhood/ZIP.

Which would you prefer?
